sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ten articles listed (Blench; Kropp Dakubu; Tutrugbu, Lelemi, Tuwuli, Logba, Foodo, Likpe, Ikposo papers); none on Animere apart from Blench's comparative paper.

sources.citation: Essegbey, James, Bryan Gelles, Felix K. Amika, Prosper Teye Akortia & Freda Asante Kumi. ELAR collection dk0331 'Documentation of Animere in Kecheibi and Kunda' (Univ. of Florida / Accra College of Education). https://www.elararchive.org/dk0331/; hdl:2196/fbd23548-859b-426d-9e96-72173f0804a6
sources.note: Collection landing page (automated download blocked 403; read via direct download twice) gives only a consonant/vowel-to-orthography table (ŋ, ɛ, ɔ, ɪ, ʊ, kw, gw, tɕ, dʑ..); the words tone/tonal/stress/accent/pitch/prosody do not occur on the page. 29 bundles of audio/video with ELAN files; no grammar sketch, phonology write-up or dictionary listed.
No phonology, tone or stress information; bibliography lists Heine 1968, Seidel 1898, Sommer 1992, Blench 2006 ms., Bodomo 1996, and the ELAR deposit 0331.

sources.citation: Dompey, Princess Enyonam, Sun Li & Francis Baidoo Jnr. 2024. Factors contributing to the decline of Animere language in Ghana. International Journal of Science and Research Archive 13(2): 1132-1147. doi:10.30574/ijsra.2024.13.2.2260
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic interview study; no stress statement. Only generic second-hand remark, section 2.4.4 (p. 1135): 'The GTM languages, including Animere, are characterized by complex tonal systems' (citing Ford & Iddah 2008 on Siwu, not Animere data). Interviewee quotes mention 'tonal variations' (pp. 1141-1142).

sources.citation: Ameka, Felix K. 2018. From comparative descriptive linguistic fieldwork to documentary linguistic fieldwork in Ghana. Language Documentation & Conservation Special Publication 15: 224-239. hdl:10125/24824
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; only records that James Essegbey and Bryan Gelles have an in-progress ELDP/ELAR + DEL-NSF multi-media documentation of Animere (table and text, pp. ~229-232).

sources.citation: ELDP funded-projects list (eldp.net): Animere, Ghana - Bryan Gelles, University of Florida, 2012; Animere, Ghana - Felix Ameka, Accra College of Education, 2024
sources.note: Grant register only; identifies the depositors of the ELAR material. No linguistic content.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2009. Do the Ghana-Togo Mountain languages constitute a genetic group? Journal of West African Languages 36(1-2): 19-35.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or on the prosodic system. Comparative tables (pp. 23-30) give Animere lexical forms with tone marks (e.g. kɪkâʔ, fùrúbí/àfùrúbí, tǔ/àtǔ, ǹdǎŋ), i.e. the data are transcribed as tonal; the words 'stress', 'accent', 'tone' do not occur in the running text. Bibliography lists Casali ined.a 'Animere wordlist' and ined.b 'Preliminary observations on the phonology and noun class system of Animere' and Westermann 1933a.
